reconcile.connective: Defenders note that Hebrew "son" routinely means descendant, so calling Jehu "son of Nimshi" simply names his grandfather as ancestor.

discrepancy.connective: Steve Wells of the Skeptic's Annotated Bible presses the plain wording: one verse makes Jehu Nimshi's son, the other his grandson, of the same man in the same story.

skeptic.name: Steve Wells
skeptic.work: The Skeptic's Annotated Bible, "Was Jehu the son or grandson of Nimshi?" (skepticsannotatedbible.com/contra/jehu.html)
skeptic.attribution: Steve Wells, The Skeptic's Annotated Bible (skepticsannotatedbible.com/contra/jehu.html)

excerpts.excerpt_text: This was a son of Jehoshaphat, and a grandson of Nimshi …
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly resolves the son-vs-grandson wording by naming the intervening generation: Jehu is son of Jehoshaphat and grandson of Nimshi, so '1 Kgs son of Nimshi' = ancestor/grandson. Only gathered voice that engages the genealogical tension verbatim. Truncated at a source semicolon -> ' …'.

pd_work.resource: John Gill, Exposition of the Entire Bible (1746-63), on 1 Kings 19:16
pd_work.author: John Gill
pd_work.note: Gill keys the harmonization to this passage, stating Jehu 'was a son of Jehoshaphat, and a grandson of Nimshi' so the shorter '1 Kgs son of Nimshi' names the grandfather as ancestor.

link.note: No allowlisted page (gotquestions.org / carm.org / defendinginerrancy.com) engages this exact tension; the only on-topic article (The Domain for Truth) is off-allowlist, so the link is omitted.
